title: Supply-shock resilience simulator and enterprise fallback decision matrix
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: Create an operational decision tool and simulation harness that helps PMs and customers (sales/solutions) choose fallback strategies when primary model variants become unavailable or economically infeasible. Scope: 1) Scenario generator for model-supply shocks (provider outages, regional capacity constraints, sudden price spikes, deprecation). 2) Cost-latency-quality tradeoff matrix populated with empirical benchmarks and heuristics. 3) Decision tree / step-by-step playbook for enterprise runbooks (what to route to, when to throttle, when to switch to quantized variants or host fallbacks). 4) Short docs for customers and internal sales/solutions engineers explaining choices and SLA implications. Deliverables: - Simulation harness (CSV and dashboard outputs) that can run N scenarios and produce expected cost delta, p50/p95 latency changes, and quality regressions (via sample prompt set). - Fallback decision matrix in spreadsheet and as an interactive console widget (MVP). - PRD and runbook pages for Solutions + GTM. Acceptance criteria: - Simulation reproduces 3 historical incidents (internal incident logs) within 10% of observed latency/cost impact. - Decision matrix recommends fallback that meets customer-defined constraints (latency SLO, max cost uplift) in >85% of test scenarios. - Documentation and quickstart for Solutions, 1 pager for Sales. Approach: - Start with model variants in our catalog (hosted/dedicated/private) and define fault modes: total outage, degraded throughput, price surge, region-level throttling. - For each mode generate synthetic workloads using representative enterprise prompt sets (RAG, chat, embeddings). - Use existing telemetry and perf-benchmarks (Console dashboards) to parameterize simulator. - Integrate quality delta estimates using A/B prompt battery from Research. - Produce a ranked list of viable fallbacks with estimated cost, latency, and quality delta. Risks and trade-offs: - Quality delta estimates are noisy for new open models; mitigate by conservative penalty factors and clear uncertainty bands. - Simulator depends on accurate telemetry for hosted partners; fallback logic must allow manual override. - Timebox: deep model-specific tuning will be deferred to follow-up epics. Stakeholders: - Product: Ava Chen (lead), Diego Martinez (owner) - Engineering: Reliability (ENG-2190), Serving Runtime (ENG-3215) - Research: Eval owners for prompt sets - Solutions & Sales: Liz Ortega, Marco Singh - Legal/Security: validation for enterprise runbooks Metrics: - Simulation coverage (# scenarios run, scenario diversity) - Decision accuracy vs postmortem outcomes - Time-to-recommendation for a given incident (sprint goal: <10 minutes for MVP) - Adoption: Solutions playbook usage in 3 pilot accounts Timeline: - Feb 12: kickoff and scoping - Feb 20: telemetry mapping and initial dataset - Mar 3: first simulator prototype and internal demo - Mar 10: pilot with Solutions + 2 pilot customers - Mar 31: MVP release to internal docs and console widget (beta)
